proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Coast Guard fleet be sized for great-power competition and home waters, with the mission set scaled to long-term congressional budgets and any added money going to acquisitions directed by an updated Fleet Mix Analysis. It asks that the Coast Guard submit a long-range shipbuilding plan to Congress, modeled on the Navy's 30-year plan. It says the Arctic mission needs funding above current levels if the Coast Guard keeps it, with a shift of that mission to the Navy to be considered.

status_summary: Public Law 119-21, approved 2025-07-04, included a Coast Guard mission readiness section (Sec. 40001), and CRS reports about 24.59 billion dollars in reconciliation funds for the Coast Guard. The Coast Guard awarded contracts on 2025-12-29 for up to six Arctic Security Cutters and on 2026-02-11 for up to five more, completing an initial order of 11; the Commandant told the Senate on 2026-01-29 that the reconciliation law also funds Offshore Patrol and Fast Response Cutters and that the service plans to grow by 15,000 people under Force Design 2028. Division G of Public Law 119-60 (approved 2025-12-18, the FY2026 defense authorization) is titled the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 and requires regular Polar Security Cutter updates; no required long-range shipbuilding plan or Fleet Mix Analysis section was identified, and the Arctic mission stays with the Coast Guard.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was approved, with a Title IV section on Coast Guard mission readiness; CRS reports about 24.59 billion dollars in reconciliation funds for the Coast Guard, split between operations and procurement.

The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (Public Law 119-60) was enacted with Division G titled the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, including a requirement for regular Polar Security Cutter updates (Sec. 7117).
The Coast Guard announced contracts for up to six Arctic Security Cutters: up to two with Rauma Marine Constructions in Finland and up to four with Bollinger Shipyards Lockport in Louisiana.
The Coast Guard announced a contract with Davie Defense for up to five more Arctic Security Cutters, completing an initial order of 11.

title: Rebuild the Coast Guard fleet, require a shipbuilding plan, fund the Arctic mission
uncertainties: The stand-alone Coast Guard Authorization Act bills (S. 524, passed the Senate 2025-03-05; H.R. 4275, passed the House 2025-07-23) were not enacted as such; Division G of Public Law 119-60 carries the title, confirmed from the law's table of contents because the GovInfo page was cut short, so Division G could contain a shipbuilding plan provision under a section title that does not say so. Division G also lists annual plans for Coast Guard operations in the Pacific (Sec. 7118) and the Caribbean (Sec. 7119), which bear on the Mandate's Pacific priority (page 156) but are operational plans, not a long-range shipbuilding plan. The amounts in Sec. 40001 of Public Law 119-21 were not visible on GovInfo; the 24.59 billion dollar figure is from CRS. The Polar Security Cutter delivery date (2030) and the Force Design 2028 figure come from a news account of the Commandant's testimony, not a Coast Guard document. The Coast Guard releases did not state contract values; the first release attributes the awards to the 2025 reconciliation law. No source was found on the American Samoa facility, wartime support board or interagency maritime office recommendations.
